## Project overview

CedHealth is a public health-tracking application built with Python and Flask. Its repository contains a server application, SQLite data access, Jinja templates, a web manifest, a service worker, and a Gunicorn production entry point.

The application organizes several related health workflows behind user accounts instead of treating meals, goals, and workouts as disconnected tools.

## Problem / goal

The project’s goal is to provide one place for users to establish personal goals and record health-related activity. The interface needs to support multiple workflows while maintaining user-specific data between sessions.

## What I built

The source implements authentication and onboarding, a dashboard, goal management, meal and weight logging, workout and exercise views, favorites, saved meals, and nutrition-oriented lookup and analysis routes.

It also includes a web app manifest and service worker so the Flask application can provide an installable progressive-web-app experience.

## Key features

- Account signup, login, logout, and initial-goal setup
- Dashboard and goal-management workflows
- Meal creation, saved meals, favorites, notes, and meal-photo routes
- Weight logging plus workout and exercise views
- Nutrition search and meal-analysis endpoints
- SQLite-backed persistence
- PWA manifest and service-worker support
- Gunicorn production entry point configured through a Procfile

::: {.tag-list .tag-list-large}
<span>Python</span><span>Flask</span><span>SQLite</span><span>Jinja</span><span>HTML / CSS</span><span>JavaScript</span><span>Gunicorn</span><span>PWA</span>
:::

## What I learned

CedHealth demonstrates how a data-backed application grows beyond individual screens: authentication, persistence, navigation, and related user workflows need to work as one system. It also provided practical experience connecting backend routes, database operations, server-rendered views, and installable web-app behavior.

## Future improvements

The repository does not include a project test suite or a formal migration framework. Useful next steps would be adding route and data-layer tests, formalizing schema migrations, consolidating dependency management, and continuing accessibility review.
